title: Redwood enterprise procedures kit — company operations (2025)
author: Maya Chen
body:
> **Archived 2025-11-15:** this page is superseded by "Redwood enterprise procedures kit — company operations (2026)" and is kept for reference only.

Overview

Purpose: One place for Redwood's operational policies and process templates: access & permissions, change management, data management, procurement & expenses, vendor management and travel. Operational owners, approvers and team leads should treat it as the reference.

Scope: All Redwood employees, contractors and suppliers who request access, change production systems, handle company data, engage vendors or travel/spend on company business. Exceptions need finance-legal approval and an entry in the exceptions register.

Principles
- Least privilege with auditable approvals.
- Controls proportional to risk.
- One set of templates to speed up approvals and audits.
- Named ownership for every control.

Owners and escalation
- Policy owner: Finance & Legal (Maya Chen).
- Operational owners: People Ops (travel), Eng-SRE (infra change), Eng-Platform (deployment policy), Procurement (vendors), Security (classification & RBAC).
- Escalation: #ops-escalation on Slack; regulatory incidents go to security@redwood.com and legal@redwood.com.

1) Access & Permissions
Access is RBAC-based and requested through the Access Request Portal (ARP).
Responsibilities:
- Requester: justification and duration.
- Approver: manager or service owner, depending on resource.
- IAM admin: provisioning and audit logs.

Approval matrix:
| Resource type | Approver | Max default duration | Escalation threshold |
|---------------|----------|----------------------|---------------------|
| Non-prod cloud project | Team manager | 90 days | Security review if > 30 days or cross-team |
| Prod read-only role | Service owner | 30 days | Security review if > 30 days |
| Prod write / admin role | Service owner + Security | 14 days | Eng-SRE approval for > 14 days |
| Vendor access (limited) | Procurement + Service owner | 14 days | Contract/DPAs required for > 30 days |

Request steps:
1. Submit the ARP form with justification, resources and duration.
2. Approvers are notified; all listed approvers must approve.
3. IAM admin provisions and tags the request id.
4. Access expires at the end date; a reminder goes out 7 days before.

Review cadence: quarterly for Prod admin roles; annual certification for vendor accounts.

2) Change Management
Categories:
- Standard: pre-authorized, repeatable tasks following a runbook; no CAB.
- Normal: ticket, impact assessment, approver sign-off, scheduled window.
- Emergency: incident remediation; post-implementation review within 72 hours.

Change request template: title, owner, category, impact assessment (services/users, rollback), window, validation/smoke tests.

Approvals:
- Normal: Service owner + Eng-SRE (infra) or Product owner (API).
- High-impact (customer-facing outage risk): CAB approval; CAB meets twice weekly with async voting available.

Normal change steps:
1. Open a ticket at /tools/change.
2. Complete the template, attach the runbook, add approvers.
3. Pre-change checklist: backups, canary, synthetic checks.
4. Execute in the window.
5. Validate.
6. Close with outcome and latency/error metrics.

Emergency: tag EMERGENCY, notify on-call and #incident, mitigate with minimal scope, review within 72 hours.

Windows: no major prod releases on high-traffic holidays (Product maintains the list). Routine changes Mon–Fri 02:00–06:00 UTC and Sat 08:00–12:00 UTC; CAB handles exceptions.

3) Data Management
Classification: PUBLIC, INTERNAL (default), RESTRICTED (PII, customer data, model weights).

RESTRICTED data is encrypted at rest and in transit, kept in approved buckets and RBAC-controlled with justification. Exporting it requires a Data Use Request and DSA review.

Retention:
- Diagnostic logs: 180 days, extendable to 365 days on SRE request.
- Backups: per service SLA; quarterly restore tests.
- Customer data: per contract, 7 years max unless specified.

Breach response: contain and preserve evidence; notify Security and Legal within 24 hours; run forensics and meet regulatory timelines.

Every dataset records owner, classification, retention policy, last updated and approved uses.

4) Procurement & Expenses
Lifecycle:
1. Identify the need and an owner.
2. Raise a Purchase Request (PR) from the template.
3. Competitive sourcing for purchases > $25k.
4. Procurement checks vendor compliance (security, SOC2, DPAs) and negotiates.
5. PO issued and vendor onboarded.

Approval thresholds:
- Up to $1,000: Team lead approval.
- $1,000–$25,000: Department head + Procurement review.
- > $25,000: VP approval + Procurement + Legal.

Cards and travel expenses:
- Corporate card for pre-approved travel.
- Expense reports within 30 days of trip end.
- Receipts for any single expense > $25.
- Per diem: US domestic $60/day (meals & incidentals); international rates on the Finance portal.

Finance may audit claims for 12 months; non-compliant claims are handled with the manager and can cost card privileges.

PR example:
```
{
  "requester": "Name",
  "department": "Engineering",
  "description": "GPU cloud capacity: 4 x A100 reserved for experiments",
  "estimated_cost": "20,000",
  "vendor": "CloudCompute Inc.",
  "business_justification": "Prototype + evaluation for Dedicated offering",
  "approval_chain": ["department-head", "procurement"]
}
```

5) Vendor Management
Onboarding: intake form and risk assessment; security posture (SOC 2, ISO, pen tests); DPA and contract signed by Legal; Vendor Registry record with owner and dates; least-privilege access.

Key vendors need a documented SLA and escalation path. Strategic vendors reviewed quarterly, others annually.

Offboarding: revoke access within 48 hours of termination and confirm data return/destruction.

6) Travel Policy
- Travel Request in the Travel Portal with manager pre-approval.
- Book through preferred vendors; personal bookings reimbursed only with prior approval.
- Follow travel advisories; register high-risk travel with People Ops.
- Lodging per city band, meals per diem or itemized, ground transport by ride-share or economy rental.
- 24/7 assistance: travel-support@redwood.com.

7) Templates
- Access Request (ARP): requester, resource, duration, justification, approver.
- Change Request: owner, impact, rollback, validation, stakeholders.
- Procurement Request: requester, vendor, cost, justification, approvals.
- Vendor Intake: vendor, controls checklist, contracts, risk rating.
- Travel Request: traveler, dates, destination, purpose, manager approval.

Governance and audit
- Access grants, change tickets and procurement approvals carry a policy id and follow retention rules.
- Audit cadence: semi-annual for access, quarterly for change evidence, annual for procurement/vendors.

Exceptions: submit an Exception Request with rationale, compensating controls and an expiry date; exceptions lapse unless renewed.

FAQs
Q: Who signs vendor DPAs?
A: Legal, with Procurement.
Q: How long are provisioning logs kept?
A: 365 days.
